title: Gideon and the Debt
premise: Kestrel Montrose's quiet contract guarding a disgraced financier unravels when a stranger named Gideon arrives claiming she saved his life years ago — a favor she has no memory of — and demands repayment: stop a staged industrial accident that will kill dozens and bury evidence of her employer's crimes. As she investigates, Kestrel discovers her own security firm helped design the cover-up, and the mentor who raised her is complicit. Torn between loyalty to her found family and the truth, she exposes the plot at the dam site, losing her firm but gaining a new allegiance — with Gideon and the survivors — and learns the favor she 'never did' was actually her mother's, a debt inherited rather than owed.
about_author: Silas Ravensworth is the pen name of a former insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing 'accidents' that weren't. They write thrillers about people trapped between the paperwork and the truth.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Guarding financier Aldous Vane at a remote estate, Kestrel is approached by Gideon, who details an act of heroism she supposedly performed in Prague — a memory she doesn't share. His 'interest' is a warning: an attack at the Corren Dam, disguised as structural failure, in nine days. The beat is unease; the reader learns Kestrel's firm, Halcyon, has a contract with the dam's owners.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with one interlude from her mentor Marcus Reyes. Digging into Halcyon's files, Kestrel finds her own security protocols repurposed to enable the sabotage — and Marcus quietly redacting her access. Gideon reveals fragments of Prague: her mother was there, not her. The beat is betrayal deepening; loyalty to her found family at Halcyon begins to fracture.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Dual POV — Kestrel and the saboteur, a Halcyon colleague she trained. Kestrel races to verify the dam's structural falsifications while Marcus offers her a choice: complicity and protection, or exile and exposure. She discovers Gideon's real motive is vengeance for his brother, killed in a prior staged accident. The beat is the point of no return — she chooses truth over family.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the dam, Kestrel and Gideon confront the saboteur and force a partial shutdown, saving the downstream town but exposing Halcyon publicly; Marcus takes the fall, or chooses to. In the aftermath, Gideon releases her from the debt — it was her mother's all along. Kestrel, firmless but unbroken, starts over with Gideon and the survivors. The beat is costly, hard-won resolution.
